key_risks: Further upward repricing of US rates and the dollar could overwhelm reversal demand across all three leading candidates.
Korea, copper and mining share global cyclical exposure, so their losses could be strongly correlated despite different instruments.
The September 17 entry close may already incorporate the Korean rebound and post-Fed stabilization, leaving less subsequent upside.
Industrial production on September 18 and new-home sales on September 24 could undermine the resilient-demand thesis; their results are unknown.
market_rationale: Only 14.49% of assets have positive five-session returns, with 2.37 percentage points of active-return dispersion. The Fed hike, higher inflation projections and stronger dollar provide substantive reasons for weakness, not a blanket reversal signal. Nevertheless, resilient spending and capital investment argue against treating the largest industrial-demand-sensitive pullbacks as evidence of collapsing demand. Selective reversals have a modest edge, with substantial uncertainty and no assumption that pre-entry rebounds remain available after September 17.
portfolio_rationale: The leading candidates combine substantial relative pullbacks with independent evidence that economic demand remains resilient; Korea also has limited contemporaneous equity-market confirmation. Their reversal probabilities only narrowly clear the eligibility threshold. The ranking does not treat quality scores as business fundamentals or mechanically reward recent winners. Other pullbacks lack sufficient support to qualify, while municipal bonds offer defense rather than an overreaction trade.
